questions.q: What does an INSTEAD OF trigger do that an AFTER trigger does not?
options: It runs in a completely different database
It fires in place of the triggering action, so the real INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE never happens unless the trigger body performs it
It can only fire on SELECT statements
It runs before any transaction begins, with no access to pseudo-tables
questions.explain: Unlike AFTER, where the change already happened, an INSTEAD OF trigger replaces the action entirely — nothing is written unless the body writes it.

questions.q: What is the classic real-world use case for an INSTEAD OF trigger?
options: Logging every SELECT query run against a table
Preventing a table from ever being queried
Making a view that joins multiple tables updatable, by routing the write to the correct underlying table(s)
Replacing a scalar UDF's row-by-row execution
questions.explain: SQL Server can't automatically route a write through a multi-table view, so an INSTEAD OF trigger's body does that routing by hand.

questions.q: What happens if an INSTEAD OF trigger's body is empty?
options: SQL Server throws a syntax error at trigger creation time
The original statement runs anyway, as if the trigger didn't exist
The write succeeds against the view but fails against the base tables
The write is silently discarded — nothing is inserted, updated, or deleted anywhere
questions.explain: Because INSTEAD OF replaces the action, an empty body means the real write never happens at all — it is simply dropped.

questions.q: Inside an INSTEAD OF INSERT trigger, what does the inserted pseudo-table hold?
options: Rows that were already committed to the base table before the trigger ran
The rows that would have been inserted, for the trigger body to act on
Only the primary key column of the affected rows
Nothing — inserted is only available in AFTER triggers
questions.explain: inserted and deleted work the same way inside INSTEAD OF triggers as they do inside AFTER triggers — they represent the intended change, not necessarily anything already written.

questions.q: In the EmployeeDirectory example, why can't the view simply be updated directly without a trigger?
options: Because HumanResources.Employee has no primary key
Because INSTEAD OF triggers are required on every view by default
Because views can never contain a JobTitle column
Because it joins two tables (Person.Person and HumanResources.Employee), and SQL Server doesn't know which one a given column update should land in
questions.explain: A view built from a JOIN across multiple base tables is a classic example SQL Server can't route writes through automatically — the INSTEAD OF trigger supplies that routing logic.
